column5: Conventions: 'the base' is ARCHITECTURE.md with amendments c, d, e folded in and g items 102-110 (with J110's refinements, J111's crypt and catacomb switch, item 110 (J115) and its raised-ways revision (J116)) as the coherence pass applies them; § points into the base, 'V12 §' into this volume, 'V0n §' into another volume; ids BCR-V12-n (§10), J-V12.n (§9), T-V12-n (§7), Q-V12-n (§11); V12 is an implementer input under §17.1 (1): names no reference class, method, grammar, palette or asset; reference evidence cited by file and section only; every number quoted from a capture is a measured behaviour (§17.1 (6)); the corpus was not read: machinery and process designed from partitioned/README.md's rules alone.

Plain words: V12 sets the rule tables' numbers right and proves it against other generators (MFCG, FTG, Neighbourhood, Village Generator, Fantasy Manor) and later the owner's historical map collection, never changing how the generator works; four loops: (1) measuring references on towns whose seeds were fixed by formula before capture; only numbers cross into the product folder; (2) measuring ours with the very same code; every number has a band by one rule; nightly report 'in band', 'out of band', 'for information'; (3) tuning: a table value changed (never code) by a recorded search on practice towns, checked on a held-out set; each change a new table version declared in release notes; saved towns open exactly as made; (4) the owner's eye: sitting page at each big milestone, pairs ours vs reference, sides hidden, three questions per pair (easier to read, more like a real town, rather use), about 35-45 minutes, can be split; only the owner's answers let a milestone say 'at parity' or 'mastered'.

Plain words: tendencies not guarantees: the harness proves each leaning by counting over many practice towns (rank vs the same town shuffled at random, ties broken by a fair coin; counting members exactly; watching a rate climb as towns grow), rules worked out beforehand so chance almost never passes and a real leaning almost always does; a failing bar re-runs once on fresh towns before anything changes; where the owner's volume states how a bar passes, that wins. Owner's rules stay the owner's (catacomb only under a cemetery, cathedral always crypted, raised ways only in cities): no tuning, fallback or historical map moves them; a historical counter-example goes to the owner as a question with 'keep the rule'; catacombs checked never to shrink on every rebuild (epoch, regeneration, re-derive, New random, upgrade) and to fill ossuaries when they cannot grow.

Plain words: later the historical maps adjust default numbers and bands, never machinery; one historical example proves possible, never common; only a fair pre-chosen sample of measured plans says how common; collection teaches drawing, never naming; its 53 held-back plates never used; MFCG and FTG behaviour stays exactly reachable through the parity presets; historical values arrive as a 'historical' layer and the owner decides at a before-and-after sitting whether it becomes default. Item 110: terraces, raised ways, decks, stepped temples measured against our own rules, not a reference; parity presets never show them; a second test city from an original sketch (port with sea-anchored wall, walled harbour, terraces, raised road, stepped temple) must come out as sketched every time, as must the first; turning the new rules off gives back exactly yesterday's towns; six short items at the M4 sitting.

Plain words: owner experience: one-page dashboard after each nightly run; a sitting page at M1, M2b, M4 (with six item-110 items), M5, M6 (buildings), the village milestone and after the historical reconciliation, shorter ones for floor plans, underground, floating islands, town histories; never more than one older unrated sitting carried into a new one; release notes name every number that moved, what it was matched against and by how much, one plain line per new behaviour switched on.

Built to depth: calibration harness end to end: metric suite as a registry with one implementation run on every source (§2.1-§2.2, §3.4); numbers-only firewall crossing (§3.3); capture-and-measure loop with pre-registered seeds (§3.2); exact band arithmetic and parity run (§3.5); correlation harness for every 'above a random baseline' bar (§3.6) and share, sweep, paired and two-sample harness of every other tendency bar (§3.6b); tuning runs as table-version bumps with declared shifts and goldens (§3.7); reference drift (§3.8); owner's sittings as a general panel engine with its page (§3.9); corpus reconciliation as a process (§3.10); calibration register (§3.11); known-city fixtures' engine, the second fixture's structure list, seed and golden (§3.14, item 110 (e)); the no-op pin engine (§3.7.8) and four feature switch-on bumps (§3.7.6).

Two derived features for sources lacking them (MFCG exports no blocks or lanes; a corpus plate may show buildings only): cluster blocks: footprints whose rings lie within g of each other join one cluster (g = 1.0 m metric, 2% of median footprint short side relative); outline = union closed by dilation then erosion of 3 m (metric) or 10% of that short side (relative); derived street graph: inside the outermost curtain (or built area's outline) the complement of cluster blocks reduced to its straight skeleton (§3.8 kernel), spurs < 8 m (metric) or 40% of median short side (relative) pruned, nodes within 2 m merged; a metric reading blocks or lanes on MFCG reads these and the same metric on our side reads the same derivation from our footprints (never true blocks) (blockc.*, sgd.*); our true blocks and ways feed rows whose reference has them (J-V12.5).

Catalogue conventions: where the base defines a measure the row cites it; m = metric scale needed, f = scale-free; every wall row reads the §2.2 enclosure (item 106): inside the outermost curtain = inside the outermost enclosure; curtain ring's area = enclosure's area; along-curtain distances along built stretches only, never across a closure edge (a condition run's end is no stretch end); a main gate is a gate of class land (a water gate, a harbour-mouth chain included, never counts).

Default rules: absFloor shares, ratios, rank statistics 0.02; angles 1 deg; lengths 2% and areas 5% of reference median; densities 5% of it; counts 0.5; Moran's I and Spearman 0.05; entropies 0.05 bits; timings 5%; sign any for Moran's I, Spearman, z, signed angles, positive otherwise; distribution bins: areas log-spaced 24 bins (blocks 50-50 000 m2; buildings 10-2 000 m2; plots 20-5 000 m2) with underflow and overflow; run lengths 5 m bins to 400 m; NN distances 0.25 m bins to 30 m; widths 0.25 m bins to 30 m; tolerance geo, model, trace, counts 1e-9 relative, render 0.01 absolute, M-1 twin comparison 0.5% relative or one unit of last printed digit; stages: ways S3, S4, S5, S8; walls, towers, gates, castle, closures, enclosures S3-S5; districts and squares S3, S6-S7b; blocks S8-S9; plots S8-S10; buildings S10-S11; water, river, pier S1 and S3; green, field, tree S12-S12a; galleries and chambers the underground stages (II.7); retaining walls S10-S11; raised parts, supports, spans S4-S6 (viaducts S4, elevated roads and aqueducts end of S6).

Estimators: a reference's per-seed statistics s1..sn give spread [a, b] and centre c (median): n = 1 -> a = b = c (single); 2 <= n < 10 -> [min, max] (minmax); n >= 10 -> p10 and p90 by linear interpolation (Hyndman and Fan type 7); with n i.i.d. draws [min, max] covers on average (n - 1)/(n + 1) (0.82 at n = 10), so at ten seeds the two aim at the same interval as §13.5's [p10, p90] (J-V12.3).

Scalar target bands: positive metric: lo = min(a x 0.9, c x 0.85), hi = max(b x 1.1, c x 1.15) (union of §13.5's rule and its single-value +-15%; n = 1 reduces exactly to §13.5's single-value rule); then lo <= c - absFloor and hi >= c + absFloor enforced; sign any: w = max(b - a, absFloor), lo = a - 0.1 w, hi = b + 0.1 w; ours = median of our per-seed statistics; a target row passes when lo <= ours <= hi (J-V12.6).

Distribution target bands: reference seed-to-seed spread = p90 (type 7) of two-sample KS distances over its n(n - 1)/2 seed pairs (n = 2 the one value); ours = median over every (our seed j, reference seed i) pair of KS(tj, si); row passes when ours <= 1.25 x that spread (J-V12.7); at n = 1: ceiling = KS critical value c(0.01) x sqrt((n1 + n2)/(n1 n2)), c(0.01) = 1.628, n1 the one reference seed's element count, n2 our median-sized seed's.

Weakness, descriptive and declared exceptions: a weakness row compares ours (median) with its one-sided bound and margin as §13.5 states; a descriptive row is reported and gates nothing; a row whose band §13.5 or a volume declares as an exception (organic turning's 0.5-1.5 x FTG; V02's chi-square and KS clauses for FM's small sample) carries that band as band.override and the report prints 'declared exception'.
